hints: Remember what a very large or very small Kc tells you about where the equilibrium position lies.
Both K1 and K2 are very small, but AgCl dissolves in ammonia while AgI does not, so think about which solid produces more Ag+ ions.
Combine the complex ion formation with each dissolving equilibrium to see why removing Ag+ can pull one solid into solution but not the other.
walkthrough:
**Link Kc size to equilibrium position**

Think simply. If equilibrium lies well to the left, there are very few products, so Kc is much less than 1. If it lies to the right, there are lots of products, so Kc is much greater than 1.

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{products}]}{[\text{reactants}]}$$

**Place K3 as the largest**

The question tells us the complex ion equilibrium lies to the right. That means lots of $\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2^+$ is formed, so K3 must be large.

$$\text{Ag}^+(aq) + 2\text{NH}_3(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag(NH}_3)_2^+(aq) \quad K_c = K_3 \text{ (large)}$$

**Compare K1 and K2 using solubility in ammonia**

Both $\text{AgCl}$ and $\text{AgI}$ equilibria lie well to the left, so K1 and K2 are both very small. But $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in ammonia and $\text{AgI}$ does not.

Ammonia removes $\text{Ag}^+$ to form the complex ion. This can only pull the $\text{AgCl}$ equilibrium to the right if $\text{AgCl}$ already supplies more $\text{Ag}^+$ than $\text{AgI}$ does. So K1 must be larger than K2.

**Put the order together**

Smallest is K2 (least soluble), middle is K1 (slightly more soluble), largest is K3 (lies to the right).

$$K_2 < K_1 < K_3$$

options.A: Incorrect. K3 cannot be smallest because its equilibrium lies to the right, so K3 must be large, not small. This option also reverses K1 and K2.
options.B: Incorrect. K3 cannot be smallest for the same reason, it lies to the right. It also puts K2 as largest, but AgI is the least soluble solid and will not even dissolve in ammonia.
options.C: Correct. K2 is smallest because AgI is least soluble and will not dissolve in ammonia. K1 is next because AgCl is slightly more soluble and does dissolve in ammonia. K3 is largest because that equilibrium lies to the right.
options.D: Incorrect. It correctly puts K3 as largest, but swaps K1 and K2. Since AgCl dissolves in ammonia and AgI does not, K1 must be greater than K2, not smaller.
